items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: So, and you know you’ve got a big band, Tito Puente, five saxes, four trombones, four trumpets, timbale, bongo, two singers you know, so it’s a full force.

ctx.x: Not the metal one with the pads. So, and you know you’ve got a big band, Tito Puente, five saxes, four trombones, four trumpets, timbale, bongo, two singers you know, so it’s a full force. And that’s a different way of playing that, see? So this is what has to be first of all, taught for us, so you’re not watering down — if you know certain things a little, at least 101, in a montuno, know a couple of timbao, like we did yesterday at the class, the second thing. We did that C7 montuno with Victor. See, that’s a…
What do you do if you get called to play like a piano trio gig plus percussion and it’s going to be mostly swing music? I mean is that harder to fit into?
